```{r Step 1, include=TRUE}

# ============================================================
# CONSTRUCT AUTHORITATIVE INDUSTRY-YEAR JQI
# ============================================================

library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(gssrdoc)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Load industry-year component panel
# ------------------------------------------------------------

industry_jqi <- read_csv(
  here(
    "01_tidydata",
    "industry_year_job_quality_2000_2024.csv"
  )
)

gss_jqi_analysis <- read_csv(here("01_tidydata","GSS_Data_Cleaned","gss_jqi_analysis_2004_2024.csv"))

glimpse(industry_jqi)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Standardize the five underlying indicators
#
# Higher values always indicate better job quality:
#
# wage_premium             = higher is better
# wage_cost_per_hour       = higher is better
# benefits_nonrequired     = higher is better
# layoffs_discharge_rate   = LOWER is better -> reverse
# earnings_volatility      = LOWER is better -> reverse
# ------------------------------------------------------------

job_quality_dimensions <- industry_jqi %>%
  mutate(
    z_wage_premium =
      as.numeric(scale(wage_premium)),

    z_ecec_wage =
      as.numeric(scale(wage_cost_per_hour)),

    z_benefits =
      as.numeric(scale(benefits_nonrequired)),

    z_stability =
      as.numeric(scale(-layoffs_discharge_rate)),

    z_earnings_stability =
      as.numeric(scale(-earnings_volatility))
  ) %>%
  
  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # 3. Construct four substantive dimensions
  #
  # Compensation = average of wage premium and ECEC wage
  # Benefits     = benefits
  # Stability    = employment stability
  # Earnings     = earnings stability
  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  
  mutate(
    compensation = rowMeans(
      cbind(
        z_wage_premium,
        z_ecec_wage
      ),
      na.rm = FALSE
    ),

    benefits = z_benefits,

    stability = z_stability,

    earnings_stability = z_earnings_stability
  ) %>%
  
  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # 4. Equal-weight the four dimensions
  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  
  mutate(
    jqi = rowMeans(
      cbind(
        compensation,
        benefits,
        stability,
        earnings_stability
      ),
      na.rm = FALSE
    )
  ) %>%
  
  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # 5. Standardize the composite across the external panel
  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  
  mutate(
    jqi_z = as.numeric(scale(jqi))
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Verify the JQI construction
# ------------------------------------------------------------

job_quality_dimensions %>%
  summarise(
    n = sum(!is.na(jqi)),
    jqi_mean = mean(jqi, na.rm = TRUE),
    jqi_sd = sd(jqi, na.rm = TRUE),
    jqi_z_mean = mean(jqi_z, na.rm = TRUE),
    jqi_z_sd = sd(jqi_z, na.rm = TRUE)
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Verify the expected complete-JQI coverage
# ------------------------------------------------------------

job_quality_dimensions %>%
  summarise(
    complete_jqi = sum(!is.na(jqi)),
    total = n()
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 8. Check the industry-year structure
# ------------------------------------------------------------

job_quality_dimensions %>%
  count(year, industry_common) %>%
  filter(n > 1)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Continuous JQI distribution by year
# ------------------------------------------------------------

industry_jqi <- job_quality_dimensions

jqi_year_summary <- industry_jqi %>%
  filter(!is.na(jqi_z)) %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(
    n_industries = n(),
    mean_jqi = mean(jqi_z, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_jqi = sd(jqi_z, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_jqi = min(jqi_z, na.rm = TRUE),
    p25_jqi = quantile(jqi_z, .25, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_jqi = median(jqi_z, na.rm = TRUE),
    p75_jqi = quantile(jqi_z, .75, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_jqi = max(jqi_z, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(jqi_year_summary, n = 30)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Define "quality industry" within each year
#
# Top 25% of industries in that year.
# This is a relative measure: an industry can be a
# quality industry in one year and not another.
# ------------------------------------------------------------

industry_jqi <- industry_jqi %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  mutate(
    jqi_year_quartile = ntile(jqi_z, 4),
    quality_industry = if_else(
      jqi_year_quartile == 4,
      1L,
      0L
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup()


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Which industries are "quality industries" over time?
# ------------------------------------------------------------

quality_industry_summary <- industry_jqi %>%
  filter(!is.na(jqi_z)) %>%
  group_by(industry_common) %>%
  summarise(
    years_observed = n(),
    years_quality = sum(
      quality_industry == 1,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    pct_years_quality = 100 * mean(
      quality_industry == 1,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    mean_jqi = mean(jqi_z, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(mean_jqi))

print(quality_industry_summary, n = 30)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Industry trajectories
# ------------------------------------------------------------

industry_trajectory <- ggplot(
  industry_jqi %>%
    filter(!is.na(jqi_z)),
  aes(
    x = year,
    y = jqi_z,
    group = industry_common
  )
) +
  geom_line(alpha = .6) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Year",
    y = "Objective job quality (JQI)",
    title = "Objective job quality across industries, 2000–2024"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

ggsave(
  here("04_figures", "TrajectoryofJQI.png"),
  plot = industry_trajectory
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. JQI distribution by year
#
# This shows how much the cross-industry distribution shifts
# over time rather than only showing the mean.
# ------------------------------------------------------------

jqibyyear <- ggplot(
  industry_jqi %>%
    filter(!is.na(jqi_z)),
  aes(
    x = factor(year),
    y = jqi_z
  )
) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Year",
    y = "Objective job quality (JQI)",
    title = "Distribution of objective job quality across industries"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

ggsave(
  here("04_figures", "JQIbyYear.png"),
  plot = jqibyyear
)
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Heatmap: industry × year
# ------------------------------------------------------------

jqiheatmap <- ggplot(
  industry_jqi %>%
    filter(!is.na(jqi_z)),
  aes(
    x = year,
    y = reorder(industry_common, jqi_z, FUN = mean),
    fill = jqi_z
  )
) +
  geom_tile() +
  labs(
    x = "Year",
    y = "Industry",
    fill = "JQI",
    title = "Objective job quality across industries and over time"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

ggsave(
  here("04_figures", "JQIHeatmap.png"),
  plot = jqiheatmap
)
# ============================================================
# PART II: ASSIGN JQI AND QUALITY-INDUSTRY STATUS TO GSS
# ============================================================

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 8. Start from the GSS JQI analysis dataset
# ------------------------------------------------------------

gss_jqi_distribution <- gss_jqi_analysis %>%
  select(
    everything()
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    quality_industry = case_when(
      !is.na(jqi_z) &
        !is.na(year) &
        !is.na(industry_common) ~
        industry_jqi$quality_industry[
          match(
            paste(year, industry_common),
            paste(
              industry_jqi$year,
              industry_jqi$industry_common
            )
          )
        ],
      TRUE ~ NA_integer_
    )
  )


# Check assignment
gss_jqi_distribution %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    jqi_available = sum(!is.na(jqi_z)),
    quality_industry_available =
      sum(!is.na(quality_industry)),
    quality_industry_n =
      sum(quality_industry == 1, na.rm = TRUE)
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 9. Distribution of GSS respondents across quality industries
# ------------------------------------------------------------

gss_quality_by_year <- gss_jqi_distribution %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(quality_industry)
  ) %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    quality_industry_n =
      sum(quality_industry == 1),
    pct_quality_industry =
      100 * mean(quality_industry == 1),
    mean_jqi = mean(jqi_z, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_jqi = median(jqi_z, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(gss_quality_by_year, n = 30)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 10. Plot proportion of GSS respondents in quality industries
# ------------------------------------------------------------

highjqidistribution <- ggplot(
  gss_quality_by_year,
  aes(
    x = year,
    y = pct_quality_industry
  )
) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = gss_quality_by_year$year
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "GSS year",
    y = "Percent in top-quartile JQI industries",
    title = "Share of GSS respondents employed in relatively high-quality industries"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

ggsave(
  here("04_figures", "QualityJQIIndex.png"),
  plot = highjqidistribution
)

```

```{r Race Descriptives, include=TRUE}

# ============================================================
# BLACK / NON-BLACK JQI COMPARISON
# ============================================================

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Create Black / Non-Black indicator
#
# racecen1:
#   1 = White
#   2 = Black or African American
#   3-16 = other valid racial categories
#
# Black = 2
# Non-Black = all other valid race categories
# Missing/unusable race codes remain NA.
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# ============================================================
# BLACK / WHITE / OTHER RACE STRATIFICATION
# ============================================================

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Create mutually exclusive race groups
#
# racecen1:
#   1 = White
#   2 = Black or African American
#   3+ = other valid racial categories
#
# Missing/unusable values remain NA.
# ------------------------------------------------------------

gss_jqi_distribution <- gss_jqi_distribution %>%
  mutate(
    race_group_3 = case_when(
      racecen1 == 1 ~ "White",
      racecen1 == 2 ~ "Black",
      !is.na(racecen1) ~ "Other",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )


# Check the three-category distribution
gss_jqi_distribution %>%
  count(race_group_3, sort = TRUE)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Create the two binary comparisons
# ------------------------------------------------------------

gss_jqi_distribution <- gss_jqi_distribution %>%
  mutate(
    
    # Black vs. White
    black_white = case_when(
      racecen1 == 2 ~ "Black",
      racecen1 == 1 ~ "White",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    
    # Black vs. everyone else
    black_nonblack = case_when(
      racecen1 == 2 ~ "Black",
      !is.na(racecen1) ~ "Non-Black",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )


# Check both samples
gss_jqi_distribution %>%
  count(black_white, sort = TRUE)

gss_jqi_distribution %>%
  count(black_nonblack, sort = TRUE)


# ============================================================
# BLACK vs. WHITE
# ============================================================

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Mean JQI by Black/White and year
# ------------------------------------------------------------

jqi_black_white_year <- gss_jqi_distribution %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(jqi_z),
    !is.na(black_white)
  ) %>%
  group_by(year, black_white) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_jqi = mean(jqi_z, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_jqi = sd(jqi_z, na.rm = TRUE),
    se_jqi = sd_jqi / sqrt(n),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    ci_low = mean_jqi - 1.96 * se_jqi,
    ci_high = mean_jqi + 1.96 * se_jqi
  )

print(jqi_black_white_year, n = 100)


m_jqi_black_white_interaction <- lm(
  jqi_z ~ black * factor(year),
  data = gss_jqi_distribution %>%
    filter(
      !is.na(jqi_z),
      !is.na(black_white)
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      black = if_else(
        black_white == "Black",
        1,
        0
      )
    )
)

summary(m_jqi_black_white_interaction)

library(emmeans)

black_white_emm <- emmeans(
  m_jqi_black_white_interaction,
  ~ black | year
)

black_white_contrasts <- contrast(
  black_white_emm,
  method = "revpairwise"
)

summary(
  black_white_contrasts,
  infer = c(TRUE, TRUE)
)


# Directly test whether the Black-White difference changed
# between 2012 and 2022

black_white_change <- contrast(
  emmeans(
    m_jqi_black_white_interaction,
    ~ black * year
  ),
  interaction = "pairwise"
)

summary(
  black_white_change,
  infer = c(TRUE, TRUE)
)

# Estimated marginal means
black_white_emm <- emmeans(
  m_jqi_black_white_interaction,
  ~ black | year
)

# Black - White difference within each year
black_white_contrasts <- contrast(
  black_white_emm,
  method = "revpairwise"
)

# Convert to data frame and retain useful variables
black_white_jqi_results <- summary(
  black_white_contrasts,
  infer = c(TRUE, TRUE)
) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  mutate(
    year = as.integer(as.character(year)),
    estimate = as.numeric(estimate),
    lower = as.numeric(lower.CL),
    upper = as.numeric(upper.CL)
  ) %>%
  select(
    year,
    estimate,
    SE,
    df,
    lower,
    upper,
    t.ratio,
    p.value
  )

# Inspect
black_white_jqi_results
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Black vs. White JQI figure
# ------------------------------------------------------------

ggplot(
  jqi_black_white_year,
  aes(
    x = year,
    y = mean_jqi,
    group = black_white,
    linetype = black_white
  )
) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  geom_line(
    linewidth = 0.8
  ) +
  geom_point(
    size = 2
  ) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(
      ymin = ci_low,
      ymax = ci_high
    ),
    width = 0.15
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = sort(unique(jqi_black_white_year$year))
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "GSS year",
    y = "Mean objective job quality (JQI)",
    linetype = "Race",
    title = "Objective job quality among Black and White respondents",
    subtitle = "Mean industry-year JQI with 95% confidence intervals"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()



# ============================================================
# Prepare controls for adjusted Black-White JQI model
# ============================================================

gss_jqi_adjusted <- gss_jqi_distribution %>%
  mutate(
    # Race
    black = case_when(
      racecen1 == 2 ~ 1,
      racecen1 == 1 ~ 0,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),

    # Continuous demographic controls
    age_numeric = as.numeric(age),
    educ_numeric = as.numeric(educ),

    # Quadratic age term
    age_sq = age_numeric^2,

    # Income:
    # inverse hyperbolic sine handles zero and negative income
    income_ihs = asinh(as.numeric(realrinc)),

    # Categorical controls
    sex_factor = factor(sex),
    marital_factor = factor(marital),
    wrkstat_factor = factor(wrkstat),

    # Year
    year_factor = factor(year)
  )


# ============================================================
# Adjusted Black-White JQI model
# ============================================================

m_jqi_black_white_adjusted <- lm(
  jqi_z ~
    black * year_factor +
    age_numeric +
    age_sq +
    educ_numeric +
    income_ihs +
    sex_factor +
    marital_factor +
    wrkstat_factor,
  data = gss_jqi_adjusted %>%
    filter(
      !is.na(jqi_z),
      !is.na(black),
      !is.na(age_numeric),
      !is.na(age_sq),
      !is.na(educ_numeric),
      !is.na(income_ihs),
      !is.na(sex_factor),
      !is.na(marital_factor),
      !is.na(wrkstat_factor)
    )
)

summary(m_jqi_black_white_adjusted)


# ============================================================
# Adjusted Black-White JQI differences by year
# ============================================================

black_white_adjusted_emm <- emmeans(
  m_jqi_black_white_adjusted,
  ~ black | year_factor
)

black_white_adjusted_contrasts <- contrast(
  black_white_adjusted_emm,
  method = "revpairwise"
)

black_white_adjusted_results <- summary(
  black_white_adjusted_contrasts,
  infer = c(TRUE, TRUE)
) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  mutate(
    year = as.integer(as.character(year_factor)),
    estimate = as.numeric(estimate),
    lower = as.numeric(lower.CL),
    upper = as.numeric(upper.CL)
  ) %>%
  select(
    year,
    estimate,
    SE,
    df,
    lower,
    upper,
    t.ratio,
    p.value
  )

black_white_adjusted_results


# ============================================================
# Formal test of the change in the adjusted Black-White gap
# between 2012 and 2022
# ============================================================

adjusted_gap_change <- contrast(
  emmeans(
    m_jqi_black_white_adjusted,
    ~ black * year_factor
  ),
  interaction = "pairwise"
)

adjusted_gap_change_results <- summary(
  adjusted_gap_change,
  infer = c(TRUE, TRUE)
) %>%
  as.data.frame()

# Inspect the interaction contrasts
adjusted_gap_change_results

#Black respondents were not consistently concentrated in either higher- or lower-quality industries relative to White respondents. Instead, their relative position changed over time. Conditional on age, education, income, sex, marital status, and employment status, Black respondents had substantially higher JQI than White respondents in 2012, but this difference had largely disappeared by 2022. The estimated Black–White gap declined by approximately one-quarter of a standard deviation between those years.


# ============================================================
# Final figure: Unadjusted vs. adjusted Black-White JQI gap
# ============================================================

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(here)

jqi_race_figure_data <- bind_rows(
  black_white_jqi_results %>%
    mutate(model = "Unadjusted"),

  black_white_adjusted_results %>%
    mutate(model = "Adjusted")
)

fig_black_white_jqi_combined <- ggplot(
  jqi_race_figure_data,
  aes(
    x = year,
    y = estimate,
    shape = model,
    linetype = model
  )
) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(
      ymin = lower,
      ymax = upper
    ),
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.35),
    width = 0.12
  ) +
  geom_point(
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.35),
    size = 2.8
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = sort(unique(jqi_race_figure_data$year))
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Year",
    y = "Black − White difference in JQI",
    shape = "Model",
    linetype = "Model",
    title = "Racial Differences in Objective Job Quality",
    subtitle = "Unadjusted and composition-adjusted Black − White differences"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 45,
      hjust = 1
    )
  )

fig_black_white_jqi_combined

ggsave(
  here(
    "04_figures",
    "Black_White_JQI_Difference_Unadjusted_Adjusted.png"
  ),
  fig_black_white_jqi_combined,
  width = 10,
  height = 6,
  dpi = 300
)

print(jqi_black_nonblack_year, n = 100)


# ------------------------------------------------------------

ggplot(

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Plot Black vs. Non-Black mean JQI
# ------------------------------------------------------------

ggplot(
  jqi_race_year,
  aes(
    x = year,
    y = mean_jqi,
    group = race_group,
    linetype = race_group
  )
) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0,

  ) +

    ),

    x = "GSS year",

    subtitle = "Mean industry-year JQI with 95% confidence intervals"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Calculate Black - Non-Black JQI difference
# ------------------------------------------------------------

jqi_black_gap <- jqi_race_year %>%
  select(
    year,
    race_group,
    mean_jqi
  ) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = race_group,
    values_from = mean_jqi
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    black_nonblack_gap = Black - `Non-Black`
  )

print(jqi_black_gap, n = 30)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Plot the descriptive Black - Non-Black gap
# ------------------------------------------------------------

ggplot(
  jqi_black_gap,
  aes(
    x = year,
    y = black_nonblack_gap
  )
) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed"

  geom_line(
    linewidth = 0.8
  ) +
  geom_point(
    size = 2
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = jqi_black_gap$year
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "GSS year",
    y = "Black − non-Black mean JQI",
    title = "Black–non-Black difference in objective job quality",
    subtitle = "Positive values indicate higher mean JQI among Black respondents"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
